announcements.headline: Amended Announcement - Multiple New Gold Targets at O'Phlay
summary: Unity Metals has identified multiple new gold targets at its O'Phlay project, expanding the exploration pipeline — however, the 'amended' nature of this filing warrants scrutiny as to what material information was corrected or added, which could affect how the market interprets the underlying quality of the target data.

With UM1 sitting more than 57% below its 12-month high, the stock is already deeply discounted relative to recent peaks, suggesting the market has aggressively re-rated exploration-stage risk. New target generation at this stage does not in itself de-risk the asset; it adds optionality but not near-term cash flow or resource definition.

At a median daily turnover of roughly A$40,891, this is an extremely thinly traded stock — volume ratios around any announcement are close to meaningless as a signal of institutional intent. Any price reaction should be interpreted cautiously, as it likely reflects retail-driven moves rather than informed accumulation or distribution.

announcements.headline: Change of Director's Interest Notice
summary: A Change of Director's Interest Notice is a routine statutory disclosure; the key detail to watch is whether the movement represents an open-market purchase (a confidence signal) or a disposal (a potential red flag), though neither fact is confirmed in the headline alone.

With MRT trading more than 51% below its 12-month high, the stock is in deeply depressed territory. A director buying shares in this context would carry meaningful signalling weight; a sale, conversely, would add further negative sentiment pressure to an already weak tape.

Until the direction and scale of the interest change are confirmed from the filing detail, the disclosure is procedural. Investors should cross-reference the form against recent capital raise activity or option vesting schedules, which can mechanically trigger director interest changes with no genuine investment intent behind them.

announcements.headline: Sky ASM and Closing Date for Directors Nominations
summary: Sky Network Television is notifying shareholders of its Annual Shareholders' Meeting (ASM) date and the closing deadline for director nominations — a routine governance milestone that signals the company is operating within its standard statutory obligations under New Zealand and ASX listing rules.

The closing date for director nominations is the operationally significant detail here: it determines whether any external or dissident nominees could seek board seats, which would be the only scenario in which this filing escalates from administrative to strategically material.

No price action data was provided for SKT, so no tape-based inference can be made. In the absence of any known activist campaign or contested board position, this filing is best treated as procedural, with attention reserved for any subsequent nominee announcements ahead of the ASM.

announcements.headline: MAP Test
summary: A filing titled 'MAP Test' under a Market Update document type is almost certainly a systems or platform test submission — it carries no investment-relevant content and should be disregarded entirely for analytical purposes.

The absence of any substantive disclosure language, combined with the generic test label, strongly suggests this was an accidental or deliberate test lodgement on the ASX platform; it conveys zero information about ZOR's operations, financials, or strategy.

Investors and compliance teams should note that test documents appearing on the live ASX feed can create unnecessary noise; the relevant follow-up action is to confirm with ZOR's company secretary that no genuine material announcement was inadvertently mislabelled or suppressed.

announcements.headline: E Map Test
summary: Like its companion filing, 'E Map Test' is self-evidently a test submission lodged to the ASX market announcements platform — it contains no disclosable information and has no bearing on ZOR's investment thesis or near-term valuation.

The appearance of two sequential test filings ('MAP Test' and 'E Map Test') from the same entity on the same date may indicate ZOR or its service provider is testing different announcement template types; this is a back-office matter with no market impact.

No price action line was provided, and none is needed — this filing warrants no analytical weight. Institutional investors should filter both ZOR test filings from their alert systems to avoid signal contamination.
